title: Tenant-aware request throttling and fallback profiles for multi-region failover
creator: Marcus Chen
description: Introduce a tenant-aware admission controller that enforces per-tenant request budgets and applies graceful degradation via fallback profiles during overload or multi-region failover. The feature combines a lightweight priority queue, SLO-credit banks, and per-tenant fidelity profiles (e.g., model-variant downgrade, response truncation, compressed embeddings) to keep high-value tenants within SLO while preserving overall system health.

acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant token-bucket admission exists and is configurable via Console (rate, burst, and priority multiplier)
Fallback profile engine supports at least three tactics: model-variant downgrade, response-width trimming, and compressed embeddings
Canary rollout shows p95 latency for top 10% tenants stays within SLO (<=250ms) under synthetic 2.5x load
No unbounded memory growth with 50k simulated tenants (validated in perf test harness)
Runbook with clear operator steps for rollback and circuit-breaker tuning is published and linked
implementation_notes: Admission controller sits in front of runtime request router; early fast-path for low-cost accepts; slow-path consults per-tenant SLO credit bank
SLO credit bank: tokens accrue at rate proportional to tenant SLA tier; credits are consumed on requests above baseline; when credits depleted, fallback profile is invoked
Fallback profiles are stored as policy templates with ordered tactics and thresholds. Profiles are evaluated deterministically to avoid nondeterministic degradation across retries
Circuit-breaker integration: admission controller exposes per-tenant circuit state. Global circuit-breakers can trigger evacuation to fallback profiles for whole-region failures
Memory optimization: use sharded LRU for inactive tenant state with configurable TTL; leverage approximate counters for large-tenant cardinality
Telemetry: expose tenant-scoped histograms for accepted, queued, degraded, and dropped request counts
testing_plan: Unit tests for admission logic and fallback selector (target 95%+ branch coverage)
Integration test with runtime router and model-variant switching in staging (end-to-end correctness)
Load test matrix: 1x, 2.5x, 5x baseline traffic; scale to 50k tenants with 5% heavy hitters; record p50/p95/p99 latencies and error budget burn
Canary rollout: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% with metric gates (p95 latency, error rate, circuit-breaker count)
Chaos experiments: simulate region outage (us-west-2) and validate automatic shift to secondary region with expected fallback profiles applied
rollback_plan: Graceful disable: toggle admission-controller=false via runtime feature flag to immediately revert to baseline behavior. Secondary rollback step: disable per-tenant fallback profile enforcement and flush in-memory policy cache. Operators must monitor p95 and error rates during rollback; if rollback triggers overload, engage emergency capacity (burst pools) and coordinate with infra to scale Dedicated capacity.
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: tenant_slo_breach_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes (severity P1)
Dashboards: per-region breakdown of degraded vs accepted requests; top 50 tenants by degraded count
SLO credit bank metric: per-tenant credit_balance gauge with aggregation percentiles
Circuit-breaker telemetry: open_count and avg_open_duration per region
